commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Re-register tables after catalog replacement (#8795)

Recover long-lived Finelog `Table` handles after a server starts with a
replacement catalog. When `WriteRows` returns namespace `NOT_FOUND`, the
handle keeps the failed batch queued, clears its registered state, runs
lazy schema registration again, and retries the same batch. The
forwarding server remains independent of Iris-specific namespace
definitions.

Before this change, the cw-us-east-08a Iris controller stayed healthy
through the node-local Finelog rollout but dropped each new
`iris.task_state` batch. The hub's last state row was 2026-08-30
16:19:09 UTC, which triggered `TrainingRunHealthDegraded` with reason
`iris_state_stale`; the hero coordinator and 176 training tasks remained
running, and Levanter metrics stayed fresh. Manual registration restored
all seven Iris namespaces on each of the three regional forwarders, and
fresh state rows from every cluster reached the hub by 16:51 UTC without
restarting Iris or Finelog.

Node-local deployment configuration now rejects `cache_pvc_name` because
that storage mode does not render or manage a claim. Producers running a
client without the re-registration behavior still require a manual
`RegisterTable` call or a restart that creates a new handle and runs
lazy registration on its first write.

The complete Finelog suite passes 116 tests, the Pulumi resource tests
pass 3 tests, and lint and type checking pass.

Incident record: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/285

Follow-up to #8789.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Use node-local caches for regional forwarders (#8789)

Run each bundled regional sender on its own bounded 250 GiB node-local
cache, expressed as both an `emptyDir.sizeLimit` and matching
ephemeral-storage request and limit. `cw-us-east-02a`, `cw-rno2a`, and
`cw-us-east-08a` no longer depend on VAST for their local Finelog
persistence path. Object storage remains the remote archive rather than
being mounted as a filesystem ahead of native object-store support.

An `emptyDir` survives a container restart within the same pod but not
pod replacement. Finelog acknowledges regional writes before the
asynchronous hub forward completes, so acknowledged rows and forwarding
cursors that exist only in the local cache can be lost when Kubernetes
replaces a pod. That is the explicit durability boundary for these
best-effort regional senders; data already accepted by the hub remains
queryable there.

The incident was a shared-storage failure rather than corrupt SQLite
state. Both `finelog-cw-use02a-cache` and its replacement
`finelog-cw-use02a-cache-20260830` used the same hard NFSv3 VAST
endpoint. Node Problem Detector reported that endpoint not responding,
and Finelog blocked in `rpc_wait_bit_killable` before SQLite catalog
initialization.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[finelog] Bound RAM when persistence stalls (#8786)

Bound each disk-backed namespace to 200 MiB of raw Arrow buffers. The
capacity check runs under the namespace insertion lock before sequence
allocation or mutation. Writes beyond the limit return Connect
`resource_exhausted`; HTTP telemetry keeps its existing retryable 503
response.

On 2026-08-30, cw-us-east-02a stopped committing flushes to its
VAST-backed cache. The process and its core-dump thread were blocked in
uninterruptible filesystem writeback, with worker threads waiting on
folios. Cgroup counters showed no OOM, and the cache used 41 GiB of its
250 GiB capacity. Ordinary requests then accumulated 8.1 GiB before
`concat_batches` overflowed a variable-width Arrow offset at
2,605,453,105; transport limits rule out one giant client update.

The existing 100 MiB segment threshold normally forces an early flush.
Capping the complete namespace buffer at 200 MiB also keeps every
production Arrow concatenation far below the 2 GiB offset ceiling. No
separate chunk lifecycle or store-wide admission mechanism is needed.

The affected PVC was deleted after the cw-us-east-02a deployment moved
to its replacement. Its Retain-policy PV is Released. The deployment
config names the replacement as the managed and mounted claim so later
rollouts retain the recovered volume.

Incident: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/285

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Drop permanently rejected forwarding batches (#8787)

Map `WriteRows` `invalid_argument` responses to permanent content
failures. Return `failed_precondition` when an incoming batch conflicts
with the hub's registered table schema. Regional forwarders advance past
permanent failures and retain schema-conflicting and retryable batches
for subsequent forwarding attempts. The entire rejected chunk is
dropped, including any valid rows it contains; those rows remain
queryable in the regional store until normal retention evicts them. Roll
the hub before senders. A new sender would otherwise mistake an old
hub's schema-conflict `invalid_argument` response for malformed content
and drop the chunk.

Every five minutes, record delta counters in `telemetry_v1.finelog` for
batch attempts and cursor sequence positions, labeled by namespace and
outcome. The fleet dashboard plots permanent, schema-conflicting, and
retryable batches, and positions dropped by permanent rejection or
retention eviction. This telemetry is itself forwarded to the hub, so
hub and network failures also delay its arrival. Operators can query
`telemetry_v1.finelog` on the regional Finelog when the hub copy is
stale.

The USE02A `levanter.metrics` summary row that exposed this behavior was
made valid separately in #8779. This contract prevents future malformed
chunks from pinning a namespace.

Incident: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/289

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Restore Kueue TAS priority preemption (#8782)

Give CoreWeave ClusterQueues binding GPU and RDMA quotas derived from
the
configured scale-group maxima. On cw-rno2a, a 1xH100 interactive
workload
remained SchedulingGated for 23 minutes while batch held about 500 of
512 GPUs;
the sentinel quotas never entered Kueue's quota-driven preemption path.

Upgrade cks-kueue to 1.5.0, which contains Kueue 0.18.3, and enable
same-cycle
TAS assignment recomputation. Kueue can now recompute a hostname
nomination
consumed by an earlier workload in the same scheduling cycle, while
binding
accelerator pressure lets LowerPriority select TAS-compatible victims.

In disposable kind, leaf-group and NVLink-domain gangs completed, and
interactive-over-batch admission produced a Kueue Workload preemption
event.
Gang restart after head preemption remains scoped to #8774.

Fixes #8781
